title: Florida Manatees Have Fans on Facebook
main_content:
A video of hundreds of Florida manatees has gone viral.

Manatees are aquatic mammals. The friendly creatures are sometimes called “sea cows.”

In the winter, the Three Sisters Springs in Crystal River is a warm-water refuge for Florida manatees. And visitors from around the world come to Crystal River for a chance to see the animals.

The weather in Crystal River has been unusually cold. On Monday, as many as 300 manatees sheltered close together in the  waters of Three Sisters Springs.

A short, 20-second video of the hundreds of manatees in Three Sisters Springs went viral on Facebook.

Just last month, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service proposed to downgrade the West Indian manatee from “endangered” to “threatened.”

While the Florida population of manatees is growing, West Indian manatees also live in the Caribbean and Central and South America. Manatee populations in other areas may face stronger threats.
